clue.text: Cordial offered by a female with improbable story

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female
a fable is a tale nobody need believe

explanation.surface: A drink served by a woman who comes with a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like the fruit drink being offered, but here it is the adjective meaning warm and friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a friendly, warm and pleasant manner towards other people.

clue.text: Praise for a Cape shellfish packed with iodine

indicators.note: packed with means filled with, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the map abbreviation for cape
a clam is a bivalve shellfish
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Compliments for a South African seafood dish seasoned with iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public approval, so a noun synonym for praise.

clue.text: Anxious about fart receiving exclamation of disgust

indicators.note: about can mean all around or askew, so these letters are moved about
receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
ugh is what people say when disgusted

explanation.surface: Someone worried about breaking wind and hearing groans of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught means tense and full of worry, so describes an anxious person or situation.

clue.text: Consecrate bishop before inferior

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
less, as in 'no less a person', means inferior or lower

explanation.surface: A bishop sanctifies something ahead of his juniors.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to make holy by religious rite, which is what consecrating means.

clue.text: Copy of book about sport reveals learning

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: an edition is a printed version of a book
RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: A sports book shows how well-read its author is.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarly knowledge, a noun for great learning.

clue.text: Cunning elder initially taken in by minor

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
something taken in is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a minor matter is a slight one
first letter of elder

explanation.surface: An older relative is outwitted by a crafty child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skill in deception, as in sleight of hand, so it is a noun for cunning or trickery.

clue.text: Walter Baskerville returned bearing weapon

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the words carry the letters within them
returned means sent back, so the letters read upwards in this down entry

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A man named Walter Baskerville comes home carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy curved cavalry sword, so an example of a weapon.

clue.text: A chit sure to be exchanged for bread and wine

indicators.note: exchanging swaps things round, so these letters change places

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A voucher that can surely be swapped for a loaf and a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament in which consecrated bread and wine are shared.

clue.text: Indian state's home to stream animal

indicators.note: being home to something means housing it inside

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An Indian state with a river teeming with wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the great apes, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Plant list developed in article

indicators.note: developed means changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the is the definite article
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A list of plants worked up for a magazine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A thistle is a prickly flowering plant, the emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Pegasus regularly goes to talk in French castle

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the winged horse's name is kept

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: The winged horse of myth keeps going off to give lectures in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French letters EAU happen to be the French word for water, which suits 'in French'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is the French word for a castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Raid suspect after taxi goes back with drink

indicators.note: going back means the word for a taxi is read from right to left
suspect suggests something dubious or unsound, so these letters are not in a trustworthy order

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police raid on a cab driver ends with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of white rum, so an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Outburst after gold set before heart of Chinese saint

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a gust is a sudden outburst, of wind or feeling
the middle three of seven letters

explanation.surface: An angry outburst after gold is set beside the heart of something Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'set before' are only order words: the outburst follows gold and comes ahead of the Chinese letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo, and the Augustine who converted England, are both canonised saints.

clue.text: State with large amount to distribute

blocks.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: A state government holds a big budget to hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions, a direct synonym for distributing.

clue.text: Worthy sacred syllable turned into recurrent theme

indicators.note: turned round means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: fit, as in fit for a king, means worthy
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice

explanation.surface: A chant of a holy syllable is turned into a repeated theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or pattern in music, art or literature.

clue.text: Dim — needing lessons about ethical dealing

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters run the other way
needing means requiring something within to be complete, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: two school subjects: art and RI, religious instruction
to dim is to fade

explanation.surface: A dim pupil needs lessons about honest business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like an adjective for a slow student, but it is the verb. RI, religious instruction, is the old British school name for RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair trade is commerce that pays producers a fair price, so a phrase for ethical dealing.

clue.text: Start made by setter setting a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themself is I
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The crossword setter begins by writing a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' often stands for I, the person who wrote the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to bring something about or set it going, a verb synonym for start.

clue.text: Mad ward with worse bad language

indicators.note: mad suggests things gone wild and out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A psychiatric ward where the cursing gets ever more foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular in form only; one swear word is an instance of bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is an obscenity, the unit of bad language.

clue.text: Toying with democratic union

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat, as in US politics
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: Someone flirting with the idea of a democratic union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toying with' looks like the whole definition, but 'with' just joins; the definition is a noun for frivolous trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual flirting or trifling, and toying is used as a noun for the same idle play.

clue.text: Swell guy stood up nurse

indicators.note: stood up in a down entry means raised from bottom to top, so read upwards

blocks.note: Sid is a typical man's name, a guy
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A nice chap stood up the nurse on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell guy' reads as a nice man; 'swell' is the verb definition and 'stood up' means jilted only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or expand outwards from pressure within.

clue.text: Reg poorly maintained by girl's generosity

indicators.note: poorly means unwell or badly done, so these letters are out of shape
maintained by means held up or kept by, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a lass is a girl; the 's is ignored in the wordplay
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Reg, unwell, is supported by a young woman's kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'girl's' reads as 'is' joining to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is liberal giving of money or gifts, so a noun for generosity.

clue.text: Animal put grand in bank

indicators.note: put in tells us to place one piece inside another

blocks.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A beast deposits a thousand at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a large striped wild cat, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: State of immature, skipping English girl

indicators.note: skipping means passing over, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: green means inexperienced or unripe
E is short for English, the letter skipped
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A green girl skips English class, out of childishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Dregs live outside university

indicators.note: outside means wrapped round, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to reside is to live somewhere
U is short for university

explanation.surface: The leftovers of student life lived off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left behind, as dregs are the remains at the bottom of a cup.

clue.text: Hold forth endlessly after getting Jesus' last fish

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter of the word is dropped
last points to the closing letter of the name it follows

blocks.note: final letter of Jesus
to prate is to talk at length, to hold forth

explanation.surface: A preacher holding forth after receiving the last fish from Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Cruel little man involved in organised crimes

indicators.note: something involved in a matter is caught up inside it
organised means arranged afresh, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
Les is the short form of the man's name Leslie

explanation.surface: A small, heartless man mixed up in gangland crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little man' means a shortened man's name, not a short man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cruel shows no mercy, so is merciless.

clue.text: Had sex with editor under rug

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means sitting below it, so the editor's letters come second

blocks.note: a mat is a small rug
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A tryst with the editor on the floor beneath a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' means placed below, so the editor comes after the rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means coupled sexually, most often said of animals breeding.

clue.text: Spiteful, topless and irritating

indicators.note: with no top, the first letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: bitchy means spiteful and catty

explanation.surface: A description of someone mean, bare-chested and annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irritating' here means causing an itch, as a scratchy jumper does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something itchy irritates the skin, so the adjective fits in its physical sense.

clue.text: Refined pin in neat fashion

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A dainty pin worn in a tidy fashionable way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' here is a verb, to shape, not the clothing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, as refined manners or taste are.

clue.text: Place to grow fruit or vegetable?

blocks.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardener asking whether a plot is for fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as a choice between fruit and vegetables; in fact the 'or' is a building block.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a piece of land planted with fruit trees.

clue.text: Drop theologian holding "back to front" view

indicators.note: back to front here means the final letter is moved round to the start
holding means wrapping round something else

blocks.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion abandons his backwards view.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'back to front' is an instruction: the last letter of the view word jumps to the front, not a full reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to go down, and drop is a verb for the same downward movement.

clue.text: Facility in which to leave oldies when rheumatoid arthritis initially returns during sad decay

definitions.text: Facility in which to leave oldies

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that precede it
returning means going back, so the letters are read in the other direction
sad suggests something in a sorry, broken state, so these letters are disordered
during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Where to put elderly relatives when their arthritis flares up amid physical decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Day care is supervised care during the day for old people or children, so a facility where they can be left.
